newsitem.title: USA: U.S. judge sentences Ferber to 33 months in prison.
newsitem.headline: U.S. judge sentences Ferber to 33 months in prison.

text.p: A Federal judge Thursday sentenced municipal banker Mark Ferber, a former partner with Lazard Freres & Co., to 33 months in prison, two years' probation and a $1 million fine.
Ferber was convicted in August on 58 of 61 fraud and corruption charges involving a contract he maintained with Merrill Lynch & Co. to advise government clients on the municipal bond market.
On Wednesday, U.S. Federal Judge William Young dropped 11 of the 58 counts during a sentence hearing.
The allegations and charges centred on whether or not a contract between Ferber and Merrill Lynch was adequately disclosed to Ferber's government clients in the municipal bond market.
Ferber had agreed to generate business for Merrill, while acting as financial adviser to various municipal issuers.

The government charged that Ferber never properly disclosed his relationship with Merrill to the issuers, which included the Massachusetts Water Resources Authority, the District of Columbia and the Michigan Department of Transportation.

Merrill Lynch and Lazard Freres settled with the U.S. Attorney's Office late last year over the matter, paying a total of $24 million in fines. Neither firm admitted or denied guilt in connection with the settlement.

Judge Young said he had originally considered a 37- to 46-month sentence for Ferber, but reduced it to avoid what he believed would be a disparity with the government's settlement with Merrill Lynch and Lazard Freres.
